Rita was the Business Manager for the Ennis Information Age Project before becoming CEO of Ennis Chamber for 13 years, a role she loved in terms of working for the benefit of Clare''s capital town. She then turning her focus to her home village of Doonbeg, where she opened a café and now runs a grocery business, employing 14 people. A dedicated community leader involved in many local organisations, she serves as a County Councillor and Mayor of West Clare, advocating fiercely for rural development.
Rita is also an outdoors enthusiast, enjoying many water activities and hiking as well as pilates. She finds peace walking Doughmore Beach and is an avid reader of the classics and Stoic philosophy. A lover of GAA football, inspired by her brother Francis’s success, she believes deeply in the social and mental benefits of sports for the community. Rita’s energy and passion drive her efforts to make West Clare thrive.
Rita was a candidate in the General Election of 2020 and is working hard with her fellow party candidates to ensure success in General Election 2024.'

'Cllr Shane Moynihan is the Fianna Fáil general election candidate for Dublin Mid-West. Since 2019, Shane has been a councillor for Palmerstown-Fonthill, representing communities in Lucan, Palmerstown and Clondalkin. A Lucan native, Shane attended Archbishop Ryan NS in Balgaddy, St. Kevin’s Community College and Coláiste Chilliain in Clondalkin. He holds a degree in Economics and Politics, a Postgraduate Diploma in Statistics, and a PhD in Political Science from Trinity College Dublin.
Shane has been deeply involved in his community for many years. He is a former secretary of his local GAA club, serves on three school boards, is a director of ACE Enterprise Park in Clondalkin, and chairs the Ballyowen Community Centre board in Lucan. Married with three boys, Shane is committed to being a strong voice for Dublin Mid-West.
His priorities include: ensuring public services work for everyone, increasing Garda presence where and when needed, delivering reliable and frequent public transport services, expanding community resources, providing more homes for young people, and guaranteeing enough local school places with smaller class sizes.
"As someone who has grown up, worked, and is now raising my family in this constituency, I understand our community’s needs. My job is to work hard for you, to listen, and to be your voice. I will never lose sight of this commitment. Táim ag tnúth le bualadh leat."'

'Aindrias has been a TD for Cork North West since the 2016 general election and a local Councillor before then since 2003.  Aindrias comes from a family steeped in public service over generations including War of Independence hero grandfather Jamie Moynihan. Married to Lisa with 4 children, Aindrias understands first hand the challenges facing young families and the importance of creating a vibrant community that can provide a first class education, affordable childcare and jobs and homes for people locally. Gaelgóir ó dhuchas as ceantair Múscraí agus ana shuim aige i ngach atá Gaelach, tír is teanga. A native Irish speaker, Aindrias is passionate about promoting our Irish identity.  Educated locally and qualified as an Engineer as well as in Marketing & Management from both CIT and UCC, he has gained experience across a range of disciplines. Living locally Aindrias is very much aware of and supports local businesses and the revitalisation of rural communities.  Aindrias believes the roll out of highspeed broadband and new technologies are key to making this happen. This will help start up small businesses and increase investment in tourism and agricultural industries in rural Ireland.  Aindrias is a dog and nature lover and is Cork to the core!'

'Michael has been a tireless advocate for Cork North West since he was first elected to the Dáil and continues to campaign for better services in rural towns and communities, such as the rollout of high-speed broadband and recreation facilities.
 
Michael is the Chairperson of the Disability Matters Committee and is passionate about improving the lives of people with disabilities. He has worked closely with families and service providers for the last 20 years on these issues, and Michael is working to keep these matters to the forefront of Government policy across all Departments.
Michael continues to operate his family farm, and has a clear understanding of the issues facing our agricultural sector – like all farmers, he loves working and farming the land, but farmers need to make a living from their work and must get a fair price for their product.
Since he was first elected, Michael has maintained a full-time constituency office in Kanturk. This office provides comprehensive advice and support to his constituents, 5 days a week with no appointment necessary.
Michael has always strived to be available to his constituents as much as possible, and through his busy office he works to help people in any way he can.'

'Jennifer has been tirelessly working for her home county since she was a child and fell in love with politics. With over two decades as a local councillor, Jennifer understands the issues that people care about most. Jennifer is well known in community and volunteer groups around the county for her work ethic and commitment. Jennifer believes in public duty and representing communities across Carlow with passion and determination. In her role as Spokesperson on Children, Jennifer works with Government to push the agenda for Children’s groups and children to the fore. She advocates for additional parental, educational and childcare supports and increased mental health supports for children. Jennifer is also the Oireachtas Ambassador for Women. She believes in an open-door policy and is fully available to her constituents and the public. Jennifer is fighting to keep Carlow on the national agenda!'

'Darragh O''Brien T.D. was appointed Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage in June 2020. He is an elected TD for the constituency of Dublin-Fingal. Prior to his election to the 30th Dáil in 2007, he worked mainly in Financial Services and was elected to Fingal County Council in 2004. He was elected to Seanad Éireann in 2011.
He has held various positions within the Oireachtas including Vice-Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee, Member of the Oireachtas Committee on Justice, Equality, Defence and Law Reform, Leader of Fianna Fáil in the Seanad, Opposition Frontbench Spokesperson on Dublin, Foreign Affairs and Housing.
Darragh’s priority is the delivery of sustainable, good-quality affordable housing to purchase or rent, built to a high standard, and located close to essential services, offering people a high quality of life.'

'Jim has been a TD since 2016. He has introduced many Bills in the Dáil, including the Parole Act 2019. He lives in Ranelagh with his family. Jim played rugby to a high level, representing UCD, Cambridge University, London Irish, Wanderers, Leinster and Connacht at senior level. He also represented Ireland at under-21 level. He holds degrees in Law from UCD, Cambridge University and the King’s Inns. He is currently Fianna Fáil Spokesperson on Justice.'

'James was first elected to Cork County Council for the Midleton (East Cork) Municipal District in the 2019 Local Elections. He went on to get elected to become one of the youngest TDs ever elected to Dáil Éireann in 2020. James comes from a farming background in East Cork. He is passionate about investment in education, transport, and health. In his role as Transport Spokesperson James wants to ensure that rural communities are not left behind. He wanted to make sure that they have the necessary infrastructure in place to live productive and happy lives. James enjoys hearing from community groups and understanding how we can work together to make Cork East one of the best places in the country to live, work and grow up in.'

'Willie O’Dea TD was born and raised in Kilteely, Co. Limerick.
 
He was educated at the Patrician Brothers College Ballyfin, Co. Laois and UCD where he studied law.
He qualified as a barrister at King’s Inn, Dublin. He has an accountancy qualification from the Institute of Certified Accountants.
He worked as both a barrister and as an accountant before embarking on a career in politics. He also spent some time lecturing in the Law faculty in University College Dublin and in the University of Limerick.
Willie O’Dea is married to Geraldine Kennedy. He writes occasionally for national newspapers.
He is a former Cabinet Minister & Minister of State and served in several different Government Departments.'

'From Rathangan, living in Newbridge, Fiona was the first woman ever elected to the Dáil Constituency of Kildare South in 2016 coming from a background of working in Education, Special Olympics and as a County Councillor.
Fiona currently serves as the FF Deputy Leader in the Seanad, FF Spokesperson for Education in the Seanad, Chairperson of the Oireachtas women’s caucus, Chairperson of the all party dementia group, Head of the Irish delegation to the Council of Europe. She is also deputy Chair of the Oireachtas Education committee and Fianna Fail parliamentary party liaison with the women’s network.
Fiona is passionate about public service, champions volunteerism and the empowerment of local Government and local Communities. She is also dedicated to social justice and achieving equality. We must all contribute to community and society to make it stronger, fairer and more prosperous.'

'Caroline was co-opted onto Meath County Council in December 2023, succeeding her late cousin Cllr Damien O’Reilly. She was re-elected in June 2024 in the Ratoath LEA, representing the towns of Dunboyne, Dunshaughlin and Ratoath and the surrounding areas. 

A qualified and accredited addiction counsellor and psychotherapist, Caroline has a wide work experience in the realms of mental health and addiction therapy. She has been involved in the justice and prison systems for over 20 years and also in therapeutic programme development. Educated in NUI Maynooth, Technological University of the Shannon: Midlands and the Institute of Integrated Counselling & Psychotherapy, Caroline holds a BA in Geography and Sociology, a HDipIT, a BA in Applied Addiction Studies and a BA in Counselling and Psychotherapy. 
Caroline’s priorities are housing, transport, community development and social infrastructure, education and healthcare. She lives in Kilcloon with her husband and daughter and is looking to be elected to Dáil Éireann for her home constituency in Meath East.'

'Christopher is the Fianna Fáil TD for Cork South West, and the party’s spokesperson on Environment, Climate Action and Biodiversity as well as the parliamentary party’s Ógra liaison.
Born and bred in Clonakilty, West Cork, Christopher was a county councillor for 13 years, in which time he served as Mayor of County Cork.
Since being elected to the Dáil Éireann in 2020 he has been a strong voice for the agriculture, hospitality, tourism and live entertainment sectors, as well as standing up for fishing communities hard hit by Brexit.
Driving decisive climate action and protecting Ireland’s rich biodiversity has been a major focus for Christopher in his role as vice-chair of the Climate Action Committee.
Christopher is a keen birder and whale watcher.'

'Pádraig is the Fianna Fail TD for Cork North Central, a diverse constituency incorporating urban, sub-urban and rural. He deals witha wide range of issues that concern people. Pádraig has always hada keen interest and passion for politics and was a county councillor from 2014 to 2019. During this time, he found it very rewarding being able to help people in the community. Padraig has been a TD for the Cork North Central constituency since the 2019 by – election. In his role as Spokesperson for Special Education, he has been working tirelessly to improve ASD provision in schools and increase the support available to children. As a teacher himself for 15 years, he has a keen awareness of the challenges facing parents. Pádraig is also a member of the education committee. He is committed to representing the people of Cork North Central on these and many other issues. His interests are education, local government, housing. Pádraig is a dad and loves spending time with his family and is a keen sports man.'

'Lynda Prendergast is a dedicated and passionate Fianna Fáil candidate running in the upcoming General Election for Dublin Mid-West. A longtime resident of Citywest, she is committed to making a positive impact in the community, where she and her husband Eoin are raising their two teenagers.
Her journey as a community activist began like many others, through volunteering on different committees within the community. This grew into a leadership role as Chairperson of the Citywest Community Council. Lynda has spent years advocating for improved schools, better amenities, increased Garda presence, and more outdoor spaces.
Her commitment to community development goes beyond advocacy. Lynda is an active board member at St. Mary’s National School, a participant in the Tallaght/Citywest and Rathcoole/Saggart/Clondalkin Community Safety Forums, a member of the Tallaght Transport Committee, and a representative with the Tallaght Drugs & Alcohol Task Force. Her priorities focus on creating a reliable and safe transport system, expanding amenities, and building safer communities for all. These experiences have given her the insight to understand the real challenges our community faces and the skills needed to make effective changes.
Lynda has been actively advocating for Dublin Mid-West and recently was successful in securing two new community Gardaí for the Citywest & Fortunestown areas; strengthening local safety. She is determined to continue fighting for a balanced approach to development, ensuring that the area’s growth includes the right mix of residential homes, business opportunities, parks, and infrastructure.'

'Hailing from Portumna, Co. Galway, Anne Rabbitte entered politics in 2014 when she was elected to Galway County Council for Fianna Fáil. Two years later, in 2016, she was elected to Dáil Éireann and was then appointed to the Fianna Fáil front bench as Spokesperson for Children & Youth Affairs.
Re-elected to the 33rd Dáil in February 2020, Deputy Rabbitte was subsequently appointed Minister of State with Special Responsibility for Disabilities by An Taoiseach Micheál Martin in July 2020.
Before entering the political arena, Anne worked for a financial institution for 25 years and is a qualified financial adviser. For 3 years, Anne also ran a community childcare facility.'

'A member of the government’s Shannon Estuary Economic Taskforce, Dee spent the last five years as the Chief Executive Officer of Limerick Chamber. Prior to that she was self employed for more than a decade, running an SME in the heart of Limerick city. Her experience has given her an in depth understanding of the Midwest regional economy and a clear focus on what is needed to win further investment and jobs for Limerick.
Dee is a working parent, with children in secondary and primary school ranging in ages from 15 down to 7, and she understands the many pressures that families are coming under. 
She is the daughter of the late Brian Corbett and Valerie O’Connor (both of Corbally), married to Mike Ryan (Raheen) and grew up in Castleconnell village, with her brothers Cathal and Ruairi.
She placed third in the Limerick Mayor election, connecting with and winning exceptional support from voters'

'Brendan Smith TD, a Committed, Experienced and Dedicated Voice for Cavan/Monaghan.
Brendan Smith, T.D. is Fianna Fáil Parliamentary Party Chairman, Co-Chair of the British-Irish Parliamentary Assembly, Member of the Executive of the North/South Inter-Parliamentary Association and Member of the Oireachtas Committee on the Implementation of the Good Friday Agreement.  Brendan served as Minister for Agriculture, Fisheries and Food, Minister for Justice and Law Reform, Minister for Children and Minister of State for Food and Horticulture.
  
From 2016 – 2020 Brendan was Chairman of the Oireachtas All Party Committee on Foreign Affairs, Trade and Defence.  He was also Fianna Fáil Party Spokesperson on Education and Skills, Foreign Affairs and Trade and Border Region Development in the 2011 – 2016 Dáil term.
Brendan was first elected to Dáil Éireann in 1992, he has been re-elected for the Cavan/Monaghan constituency in each subsequent General Election. Prior to his election to Dáil Éireann, he served as a Special Advisor to the former Tánaiste and Minister, the late John Wilson.'

'Fianna Fáil blood flows deep in Niamh  as a grandniece of former Minister Paddy Smith.  Niamh is dedicated and  ambitious as your TD and  serves all constituents and Ireland with energy, enthusiasm and passion.
 
As Chair of the Committee on Media, Tourism, Arts, Culture, Sport and the Gaeltacht Niamh is provided with the wonderful opportunity to support, develop and cherish our rich heritage and evolving culture. As a people our collective experience of different traditions and beliefs is the pathway to our Shared Island.
Niamh is acutely aware of the pressing issues that are causing heartbreak and trauma to the lives of people even under the heavy cloud of Covid-19. Top of  her priorities include the reduction of housing and hospital waiting lists, the development of adequate child services, supporting farmers and fighting for the repair and upgrading of our rural roads.
 
Very much linked to these issues is the everyday concerns of people and giving all problems justified attention. Your peace of mind and personal contentment is paramount  to Niamh and she is at your service.'

'Born in Mullingar in 1982, Robert Troy is a native of Ballynacargy, Co. Westmeath. He attended Emper National School and St Finians College, Mullingar before moving to study and work in Dublin. He worked in banking and financial institutions before returning to Ballynacargy to take over the family post office in 2003 and run his own business. Robert first entered politics in 2004 when he was elected to Westmeath County Council where he served for seven years.
Robert has represented the people of Longford- Westmeath for a decade, since his election to Dáil Éireann on his first attempt in 2011. He has successfully retained his seat and was re-elected in both the 2016 and 2020 general elections. Throughout his political career, Robert’s core priorities have been promoting balanced regional development, particularly for the Midlands, and supporting SMEs as well as advocating for greater social reforms in Ireland, including migrant rights and marriage equality.
Since taking his seat in the Dáil, Robert has held a number of portfolios as a Frontbench Party Spokesperson including Arts & Heritage, Children & Youth Affairs, Transport, Tourism & Sport and most recently Business, Enterprise & Innovation. He served on the Oireachtas Committee on Business, Enterprise and Innovation and Oireachtas Committee on Transport, Tourism and Sport, and was a member of the Council of Europe.'

'Naoise Ó Cearúil has been a dedicated public servant for over a decade, first elected to Kildare County Council in 2014 at just 24 years of age. Re-elected in both 2019 and 2024, Naoise served as Mayor of Kildare from 2021 to 2022, championing local issues and working to improve Kildare. Born and raised in Maynooth, Naoise’s roots in the area run deep. Educated in Leixlip, Kilcock, and Maynooth, he has a strong connection to the local education system.
Professionally, Naoise has spent the past eight years working in the tech sector, commuting to Dublin while staying actively involved in the community. Naoise’s commitment to education has been a central focus, serving as the founding Chairperson of Gaelcholáiste Mhaigh Nuad, former Chairperson of the Board of Maynooth Community College, and a member of the Board of Management for Celbridge Community School.
Living in Maynooth with his wife and expecting their first child, Naoise is passionate about addressing key issues like childcare, social infrastructure, and the cost of living. Naoise is determined to ensure that Kildare North has the resources it needs to thrive, both now and into the future.'
